summary: Custom-node requirements reinstall the CUDA torch stack over the CPU one - the second half of MPI-406. downloadManager.js:2181 runs pip -r <node reqs> --upgrade with no index constraint, so torch comes from default PyPI (CUDA) and --upgrade replaces the correct CPU torch. Measured via ComfyUI-LTXVideo on a driverless box: torch, torchvision, triton, cuda-toolkit, 14 nvidia-* wheels. The comment at downloadManager.js:2033 asserting --upgrade is a no-op when satisfied is wrong and is why this stayed invisible. requirementsDrop cannot fix it - timm/diffusers pull torch transitively.

Implementation started. Consumer sweep done first: runPipCommand has exactly two callers, both in downloadManager.js, and the other (pipPins, :2198) already omits --upgrade. The REMOTE twin (cubric-vision-pod wrapper.py:2229) also already omits it and has run that way in production across the MPI-385 Pod sweep, so dropping it locally CONVERGES the twins rather than splitting them.
Compact plan - single Implementation item derived.

ROOT CAUSE DISPROVEN. With a correct torch 2.13.0+cpu present, dry-run of the real LTXVideo requirements with and without --upgrade is byte-identical and NEITHER installs torch/torchvision/nvidia-*. PEP 440 makes the claimed mechanism impossible: 2.13.0+cpu outranks PyPI bare 2.13.0. No pip.conf, no PIP_* env, no index directive anywhere. The CUDA stack appeared because torch was ABSENT after comfy install failed (MPI-411) and the node stage then resolved bare torch from PyPI, whose linux wheel IS the CUDA build. So MPI-413 is downstream of MPI-411, now fixed and live-verified. The --upgrade removal is KEPT but re-attributed to the MPI-217 drift class, proven separately: einops pinned to 0.8.0 would be bumped to 0.8.2 with --upgrade, left alone without. Converges with the remote twin, which never had the flag.

Evidence C appended: the cupy build failure is NOT macOS-specific. Reproduced on Windows during a live 1.3.0 portable install (RTX 4060 Ti, ComfyUI 0.29.2) with the root cause the macOS run never surfaced - cupy-wheel is a 2.9kB source-only shim whose setup.py imports pkg_resources, which modern setuptools no longer ships, so it fails on every platform on every fresh install until the curated set decides the question. Pins three requirements for the curated file: make cupy an explicit pin-or-drop rather than a leftover (never carry cupy-wheel, whose only job is the runtime CUDA detection the curated file replaces), constrain setuptools or ban source builds via --only-binary, and note this is another case of a failure reporting itself as success - 'Custom install command succeeded for ComfyUI-Frame-Interpolation' is logged 400ms after the ERROR. Severity unchanged: wasteful, not broken.

TWO REAL BUGS CAUGHT BY THE GUARD DURING THE BUILD: (1) --no-emit-package torch does NOT exclude torch transitive closure, so the first compile emitted pinned triton, 16 nvidia-* wheels and cuda-toolkit/cuda-bindings/cuda-pathfinder all via torch - this cards own Evidence A stack reproduced by our own generator; fixed by filtering the engine-owned family post-compile, keeping nvidia-ml-py which is pure-python. (2) three TRANSITIVE opencv variants (mediapipe, ultralytics, albumentations) defeated the unification and pipPins was forcing two at once, so import cv2 is last-writer-wins on every engine today - which is why --no-deps is load-bearing not an optimisation.
